extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, and policy analysts interested in Paraguay's telecommunications, media, and internet freedom
extracted.subtask_description: A country-level overview of Paraguay's telecommunications infrastructure, usage statistics, broadcast media, internet metrics, and censorship/media-regulation issues. The page compiles quantitative indicators (telephone lines, mobile subscriptions, internet users, hosts, broadcasters) and narrative on media freedom and regulatory changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-line telephone density / Fixed telephone subscriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Paraguay has the lowest fixed-line telephone density in South America, with 5.6 lines per 100 residents; Fixed telephone subscriptions: 364,557; 6.1% of the population in 2011.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an indicator of traditional telephony infrastructure and access; comparisons to neighbouring countries (Bolivia 8.7, Brazil 21.9, Argentina 24.9 lines per 100) show relative deficiency. Low fixed-line density is linked to growth in mobile usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile-cellular telephone subscriptions / mobile penetration
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile-cellular telephone subscriptions: 6,529,053; 99.4% of the population in 2011.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High mobile subscriptions are presented as compensating for meager land-line services; mobile penetration is a key metric of communications access when fixed-line infrastructure is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: State operator performance and governance (Copaco)
rubrics_metrics.description: The state-owned Corporación Paraguaya de Comunicaciones (Copaco) is known for inefficiency and overstaffing; privatization was attempted in 2002 but failed amid a banking scandal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as an assessment of institutional capacity and governance of national telecommunications provision; history of failed privatization indicates structural and political constraints on reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephony infrastructure and international connectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal switching center is Asunción; Domestic: microwave radio relay network; International: satellite earth station - 1 Intelsat (Atlantic Ocean) in 2009; International country code: 595.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the physical and international connectivity assets that determine network reach and international exchange capability; inclusion of country code and international earth station indicates routing/peering endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radio availability and role
rubrics_metrics.description: Radio is an important disseminator of information in Paraguay; Radio stations: roughly 75 commercial and community stations; one state-owned radio network in 2010; Radios: 4,475,000 in 1997.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts of stations and radios are metrics for broadcast reach and the importance of radio as an information medium, especially in contexts with lower internet penetration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television broadcast stations and household television ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Television broadcast stations: 6 privately owned and one state-owned in 2010; Televisions: 4,429,000 in 1997; 750,000 households in 2004.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcast station ownership mix (private vs state) and household TV counts measure television access and the degree of state presence in broadcasting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Households with a computer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A basic indicator of digital device penetration and potential for internet usage at home; useful when interpreting internet access and digital literacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet users / internet penetration
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet users: 1,543,715; 24% of the population in 2011 (95th in the world).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentage of individuals using the internet indicates national digital inclusion; world ranking provides comparative context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Households with Internet access at home
rubrics_metrics.description: Households with Internet access at home: 19.3% in 2011.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures home connectivity specifically (as distinct from mobile or public access) and is relevant for assessing digital divide and policy targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet hosts / internet infrastructure capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet hosts: 278,473; 64th in the world in 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of internet hosts is an infrastructure/capacity metric reflecting the scale of domestic hosting and online presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed broadband subscriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed broadband Internet subscriptions: 28,147; 0.44% of the population in 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low fixed broadband subscription rate indicates limited fixed high-speed access and helps explain reliance on other access modes (mobile, public access).

rubrics_metrics.name: IPv4 addresses allocated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPv4 allocation per capita is a measure of internet addressing resources available domestically and can reflect size of internet ecosystem and hosting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal protections for freedom of speech and press / government respect for rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The law provides for freedom of speech and press, and the government generally respects these rights in practice; Individuals criticize the government publicly and privately, generally without reprisal or impediment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as an evaluative criterion for media freedom and the legal/regulatory environment affecting communication; statements about practice vs. law indicate de jure/de facto assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government restrictions on Internet access or monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no government restrictions on access to the Internet or credible reports that the government monitored e-mail or Internet chat rooms; Individuals and groups could engage in expression via the Internet, including by e-mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit absence (or presence) of government-imposed technical or surveillance restrictions is a core indicator of internet freedom and user privacy/speech environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media crackdown and state control risks (post-2012 events)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the 22 June 2012 parliamentary coup that ousted President Fernando Lugo, the new government appears to be in the process of assuming complete control of the state-owned media and its hostility is affecting journalists with the privately owned media as well; reports of purges and firings in state media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political events and subsequent state actions (purges, firings, takeover of state media) are indicators of evolving media freedom risks and practical constraints on independent journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory changes affecting community radio and enforcement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Amended Telecommunications law clauses place a ban on advertising on community radio stations, restrict their transmission range, and open the possibility of legal action against their representatives if they broadcast without a licence; calls from broadcasters' union to withdraw licences of 'pirate' radios accused of inciting crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal/regulatory specifics (advertising bans, transmission limits, licensing enforcement) and advocacy for enforcement are criteria for assessing the regulatory environment's impact on community/alternative media and pluralism.
